name: Stop the Bus
description: Stop the Bus is a fast-paced commerce game played with 3 cards, similar to Commerce and 31. Players start with 3 lives (tokens) and aim to *not* have the worst hand when someone calls 'Stop the Bus'. The game is elimination-based, with the last surviving player winning.

content.text: Stop the Bus is a fast-paced commerce game played with 3 cards, similar to Commerce and 31. Players start with 3 lives (tokens) and aim to *not* have the worst hand when someone calls 'Stop the Bus'. The game is elimination-based, with the last surviving player winning.

Stop the Bus is a British draw-and-discard game in the commerce family. It shares mechanisms with Commerce (18th century) and Thirty-One (Scat), in which players draw and discard to improve a three-card hand. The version documented here was contributed by Nic Cleveland from Guernsey; the name is also used for a Thirty-One variant (Ride the Bus) and for Bastard Brag, which uses table exchange instead of stock and discard.
From two to around nine or more can play; the game is best with three to five. With more players, those eliminated early have nothing to do until the game ends.
A standard Anglo-American 52-card pack; cards in each suit rank high to low A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2.
Three tokens (e.g. pennies or matches) per player; optionally a small model bus to signal end of play.
Dealer shuffles and deals three cards to each player one at a time face down. The next card is placed face up to start the discard pile; the remainder is placed face down as the stock.

items.text: Bastard Stop the Bus: Variant where players exchange cards with a 3-card hand on the table rather than drawing and discarding from stock/discard. Same Brag hand ranking and elimination by lives.
